messages.author: 6027f89368dc1269
messages.subject: How to load unsupported packages.
parts:
Dear Renjine developers,

Many thanks for your project, it is great!
I have an issue using "Caret" package in my Java project. 
The error is: "Could not load package caret; tried org.renjin.bioconductor:caret, org.renjin.cran:caret" 
I went to Renjine packages directory and caret is there thouth the proplem comes from some unsupported related libraries.
Is there any way I can integrate it manually into my Projects?

Thank you very much and best wishes!

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: How to load unsupported packages.
parts:
Hi Alina,
Indeed, Renjin can't run caret due to problems building/running it's dependencies.

I took a quick look at one of the blockers, the foreach package, and updated Renjin with a quick fix, so now that at least is resolved.

The only remaining blocker for caret is then (ultimately) Matrix, which is failing due to some remaining problems with Renjin's S4 implementation:

" methods can add arguments to the generic 'toeplitz' only if '...' is an argument to the generic"
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/Matrix/1.2-3/build/13

This is something we're actively working on, but one way to help is to help reduce these kinds of errors down to simple test cases. 

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: How to load unsupported packages.
parts:
Wow, sir! Thanks so much for your kind reply. Once again, your project is  amazing! Though packages like rengine and reserve are are harder to implement, they return poor output with missing values etc. So Renjin does solve both of the issues of being able to easily run the R script and getting user-friendly output. It's a shame I can't use it in my project now , but I will definitely have a look at this error and may be will place this question in stack overflow community .
I have thought about storing caret on own server , but this is quite complicated for me and I don't know maven. 

In any case, thanks so much once again and wish you best of luck with your project. I believe the demand for it will only grow.

Kind regards,

Alina.
